data.title: Golden Minerals appoints David Watkins as CEO as Pablo Castanos steps down
data.description:
Golden Minerals (AUMN:CA) said on Friday that Pablo Castanos will resign as president and CEO, effective September 30, 2026, to pursue another opportunity. Castanos will continue to serve as a director of the Company. 

David Watkins, a director of the company since 2009, has been appointed as president and CEO of the company.

data.title: Matinas BioPharma gets 2027 window to restore NYSE American listing compliance
data.description:
• Matinas BioPharma Holdings (MTNB) announced on Friday that it received a non-compliant notice from NYSE American for falling below its stockholders’ equity requirement.
  • The company had $1.8M in stockholders’ equity as of June 30, below the required $2.0M, and has reported losses in each of its past five fiscal years.
  • NYSE American has given the company until October 2, 2027, to regain compliance under its existing plan.
  • The notice has no immediate impact on the stock’s listing or the company’s operations. However, failure to regain compliance could lead to delisting proceedings.

data.title: Ionis Pharmaceuticals falls after Pelacarsen fails key Phase 3 heart trial
data.description:
• Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS) announced on Friday that partner Novartis' pelacarsen failed to meet the main goal of its Phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial, as it did not reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events versus placebo.
  • The drug successfully lowered Lp(a) levels, but this did not lead to a reduction in heart-related events compared with the placebo.
  • The result is a major setback for pelacarsen, which was being developed for people with high Lp(a), an inherited risk factor linked to heart disease that affects about 20% of people worldwide.
  • Pelacarsen showed an acceptable safety profile, with full trial results expected to be presented at a future medical meeting.
  • Shares of Ionis Pharmaceuticals fell 6.18% to about $54.50 in after-hours trading following the announcement.

data.title: Airbus reaches preliminary deal with Spanish unions
data.description:
Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) reached a preliminary deal with four unions in Spain, Reuters reported Friday, marking a potential breakthrough in a dispute that has triggered weeks of strikes at the company's Spanish plants.

The company said it reached a "proposal of understanding" ​with unions UGT, ATP, CCOO, and SIPA after a meeting mediated by the Industry Ministry to resolve a labor dispute over ​pay and conditions following months of negotiations.

The proposal will be submitted to the ​entire workforce for a binding referendum, Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) reportedly said ​in a memo sent to its ⁠staff in Spain.

Separately, Reuters also reported that Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) has been forced to slow deliveries of its A330neo jet after a stray tool was discovered in the tail section of an aircraft in production during a pre-delivery inspection.

"We confirm we recently identified an isolated quality ​issue on an A330 horizontal tail plane," the company said in ⁠a statement. "This led us to inspect A330s in the production process, slowing ​down monthly deliveries over the summer. The root cause is identified and A330 deliveries ​have resumed."

The horizontal tail plane is made in Airbus's (EADSF) (EADSY) Spanish facilities, although the discovery ​likely is not related ⁠to the recent strikes at the company's Spanish plants.

data.title: Fair Isaac slumps 17% on VantageScore directive
data.description:
Fair Isaac (FICO), a global analytics and decisioning-software company, retreated almost 17% on Friday, after Federal Housing Director Bill Pulte directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to allow all lenders to use the competing VantageScore credit-scoring system. The directive landed as a direct challenge to FICO's pricing power in mortgage originations, one of its most concentrated revenue streams.

The stock closed at $932.26, a decline of $186.67 on the session.

data.description:
• TOP Financial (TOP) announced on Friday that it will relocate its global headquarters to Houston, Texas, as it shifts its corporate focus toward the U.S. market.
  • The company said the move will bring it closer to its AI business, strategic partners, and U.S. talent while supporting expansion in North America.
  • It will complete the relocation in phases over the coming months, with its other regional offices continuing to operate.
  • The company said the transition will not disrupt services for existing clients or partners.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Micron advances 6% as part of sector upswing
data.description:
Shares of Micron Technology (MU), a developer of memory and storage products, climbed just over 6% today, closing at $1,016.59 after rising $58.43 on the session. The advance came as semiconductor peers also posted broad gains, with AMD up nearly 5%, Taiwan Semiconductor rising almost 3%, and Astera Labs jumping almost 10%.

Other Recent News: Micron Technology

  • September 4: Seeking Alpha reported that Micron's capital spending had risen alongside broader AI-infrastructure investment, with Micron's spending cited as a significant share of sales. Read more

  • August 21: BMO Capital initiated coverage of Micron at Outperform, citing AI-memory demand, tight DRAM and NAND supply-demand conditions, and visibility from long-term and strategic customer agreements. Read more

Latest Analyst Commentary on Micron Technology

  • James Foord (September 3): Maintained a bullish view, arguing that AI-driven memory demand and customer commitments support Micron's valuation, while flagging Nvidia's potential adoption of alternative memory architectures as a key risk. Read more
  • Eric Sprague (September 3): Rated MU bullish, expecting another record quarter driven by DRAM and AI-memory demand, while noting cyclicality and potential future overcapacity from new fab additions as risks. Read more
  • Bohdan Kucheriavyi (September 2): Rated MU bullish, highlighting HBM4 demand, strategic customer agreements, and capacity sold out through 2026, while citing future supply normalization and sentiment-driven volatility as risks. Read more
  • Geneva Investor (September 2): Initiated coverage at neutral, arguing that high margins and memory scarcity are positive but that Chinese capacity growth and limited shipment growth could constrain upside. Read more
  • Yiannis Zourmpanos (September 1): Rated MU very bullish, contending that persistent memory shortages and delayed capacity additions reduce concerns about a near-term supply glut. Read more
  • Chris Bazzle (August 31): Rated MU bullish, describing Micron as an increasingly important AI-memory supplier supported by HBM demand and strategic customer agreements, while acknowledging supply-normalization and geopolitical risks. Read more
  • Hunting Alphas (August 24): Rated MU very bullish, arguing that the DRAM market should remain tighter than NAND and that Micron is well-positioned to benefit from HBM growth. Read more

What SA Users Are Saying About Micron Technology

Seeking Alpha community sentiment on Micron appeared mixed but tilted bullish, with many commenters emphasizing AI-memory scarcity, HBM demand, and long-term agreements, while skeptics focused on China competition, tariffs, technology substitution, and the cyclical nature of memory pricing.

  • One SA user argued that Micron's strategic customer agreements may reduce boom-bust revenue volatility and improve earnings visibility over time. Read more
  • Another commenter expressed concern that Micron's capital spending plans require sustained margins, emphasizing the memory industry's historical cyclicality as a risk to that assumption. Read more
  • One reader shared a bullish thesis that rising HBM capacity and memory pricing could create additional upside to future earnings estimates. Read more
  • A separate SA user questioned whether Micron's commercial pricing flexibility could hold up under negotiated long-term customer agreements. Read more
  • One SA community member raised concerns about AI-memory demand durability, Chinese competition, and assumptions surrounding future capital returns to shareholders. Read more
